definitions.explanation: A standardized application form used in Japanese job hunting. Companies require applicants to fill out an entry sheet as the first step in the hiring process, typically including self-introduction, motivation, and strengths.

examples.japanese: エントリーシートを{提出|ていしゅつ}した。
エントリーシートの{締|し}め{切|き}りは{来週|らいしゅう}です。
examples.english: The deadline for entry sheets is next week.

examples.japanese: {就活|しゅうかつ}で{何十社|なんじゅっしゃ}ものエントリーシートを{書|か}くのは{大変|たいへん}だった。
examples.english: Writing entry sheets for dozens of companies during job hunting was exhausting.

examples.japanese: エントリーシートに{自己|じこ}PRと{志望動機|しぼうどうき}を{書|か}かなければならない。
examples.english: You have to write a self-promotion section and your motivation on the entry sheet.

notes:
A wasei-eigo (Japanese-coined English) term abbreviated as ES. Central to the {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう} (job-hunting) process in Japan, where university students apply to multiple companies simultaneously. Unlike a Western-style resume, the entry sheet is a company-specific form with essay-style questions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- エントリーシートを{書|か}く: write an entry sheet
- エントリーシートを{提出|ていしゅつ}する: submit an entry sheet
- エントリーシートが{通|とお}る: pass the entry sheet screening
- エントリーシートで{落|お}ちる: be rejected at the entry sheet stage

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese {新卒|しんそつ}{採用|さいよう} (new graduate hiring), the entry sheet is the first hurdle. Thousands of students may apply to a single company, and many are screened out at this stage. Students often attend {就活|しゅうかつ}セミナー to learn how to write effective entry sheets.
